'''Gunther Siegmund Stent''' (March 28, 1924 – June 12, 2008<ref>{{cite news | first = Dennis | last = Hevesi | title = Gunther Stent, an Early Researcher in Molecular Biology, Is Dead at 84 | url = https://www.nytimes.com/2008/06/16/health/research/16stent.html | work = [[The New York Times]] | date = June 16, 2008 | accessdate = June 18, 2008 }}{{subscription required}}</ref>) was a German-American [[Molecular biology|molecular biologist]] and professor at the [[University of California, Berkeley]]. An early [[bacteriophage]] researcher associated with the [[phage group]] that formed around [[Max Delbrück]] at the [[California Institute of Technology]], he was known for his influential textbook ''Molecular Biology of Bacterial Viruses'' (1963), his studies on the [[metabolism]] of [[bacteria]] and the [[neurobiology]] of [[leech]]es, and his writings on the history and philosophy of science.

Born in [[Berlin]], Stent emigrated to the United States in 1940 to escape [[Nazi Germany]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Ávila |first=Jesús |date=June 23, 2008 |title=Gunter Stent, uno de los fundadores de la biología molecular |url=https://elpais.com/diario/2008/06/23/necrologicas/1214172002_850215.html |access-date=March 13, 2026 |work=El País |language=es |trans-title=Gunter Stent, one of the founders of molecular biology |issn=1134-6582}}</ref> He was a member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]], the [[United States National Academy of Sciences]], and the [[American Philosophical Society]].

==Life and career==
Stent was born Günter Siegmund Stensch in [[Berlin]], Germany. In 1940, he emigrated to the United States to escape [[Nazi Germany]], crossing the border over a snow-covered mountain, as he later recounted in his autobiography.<ref>Stent GS. (1998). Nazis, Women, and Molecular Biology: Memoirs of a Lucky Self-hater. Kensington, Calif: Briones Books. {{ISBN|978-0-9664563-0-1}} {{ISBN|0-9664563-0-0}}</ref> He settled in [[Chicago]] and changed his surname. He received his [[Bachelor of Science|BS]] (1945) and PhD (1948) from the [[University of Illinois]].<ref name="Squire">{{cite book|editor-last1=Squire|editor-first1=Larry R.|title=The history of neuroscience in autobiography.|url=https://archive.org/details/historyneuroscie00squi_839|url-access=limited|date=1996|publisher=Society for Neuroscience|location=Washington DC|isbn=0-12-660302-2|page=[https://archive.org/details/historyneuroscie00squi_839/page/n407 397]}}</ref>

In 1949, Stent joined the [[phage group]] that had formed around [[Max Delbrück]] at the [[California Institute of Technology]] in Pasadena. This group served as the incubator for many fundamental ideas in the emerging field of [[molecular biology]]. Drawing on discussions among group members, Stent wrote ''Molecular Biology of Bacterial Viruses'' (1963), dedicated to Delbrück, which surveyed the state of the field at that time.<ref>Stent GS. 1963. Molecular Biology of Bacterial Viruses. WH Freeman and Co., San Francisco, CA. ASIN: B002OXAPMO</ref> His later textbook ''Molecular Genetics: an Introductory Narrative'' (1971) was translated into Italian, Japanese, Russian, and Spanish.

Beyond molecular biology, Stent wrote on the history and philosophy of science. His 1969 Berkeley lectures were published as ''The Coming of the Golden Age: A View of the End of Progress''.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Stent |first=Gunther Siegmund |title=The Coming of the Golden Age: A View of the End of Progress |date=January 1, 1969 |publisher=Doubleday |isbn=978-0-385-01937-8 |edition=First}}</ref>

Stent was elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]], the [[United States National Academy of Sciences]], and the [[American Philosophical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gunther Siegmund Stent |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/gunther-siegmund-stent |access-date=May 19, 2022 |website=American Academy of Arts & Sciences}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Gunther S. Stent |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/gunther-s-stent-jhkhbu/ |access-date=May 19, 2022 |website=nasonline.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=APS Member History |url=https://search.amphilsoc.org/memhist/search?creator=Gunther+Stent&title=&subject=&subdiv=&mem=&year=&year-max=&dead=&keyword=&smode=advanced |access-date=May 19, 2022 |website=search.amphilsoc.org}}</ref> He died of [[pneumonia]] on June 12, 2008, at the age of 84.<ref>{{cite news|title=Biologist Gunther Stent has died at 84 |url=https://newsarchive.berkeley.edu/news/media/releases/2008/06/17_stentobit.shtml |website=newsarchive.berkeley.edu |date=June 17, 2008 |access-date=December 12, 2023}}</ref>

===Philosophy of science===
